Kind regards,

result.summary: I've left this routine dishwasher job in scheduling and put it on hold for 2 days while we wait for the contractor. The landlord approved attendance (event 9) and Oakfield Homes was assigned (events 11–13). The two call logs after that were a contractor phoning the tenant (event 14) and a system note about a call that didn't connect (event 15). Neither needs a reply from us. The only odd thing is that the caller gave the name "Cedar Maintenance", not Oakfield Homes. I sent Oakfield one email asking them to confirm that call was made for them and to tell us the visit date once agreed.

judgement.why_this_decision: Event 9 is a clear landlord approval ('Yes please go ahead'), approval 9 is recorded as approved, and the contractor has been assigned and notified, so the next step is for the contractor to agree a visit with the tenant. Event 14 shows that is under way: a contractor phoned the tenant to arrange it. classify_reply rated it routine scheduling (autonomy auto, needs_human_response 0.2). Event 15 is just a system note about a call that couldn't connect. Nothing here needs a reply from us. The only loose end is the caller's company name, and Oakfield can confirm that, so I asked them in one message and set a hold to chase.

alternatives_considered.option: Escalate the contractor name mismatch to a human
alternatives_considered.why_not: Different trading names for the same contractor are normal. No money, payee or scope is involved yet, and Oakfield can answer it directly.
She has already been told Oakfield will be in touch (event 12), and the contractor is already trying to reach her. Another message wouldn't move the job on.
The name mismatch should be cleared up before anyone attends, and the job needs a follow-up date so it doesn't go quiet.
